title: Grade 3 Science — Tue, May 19
description: Food and Nutrition — Last Week Day 2
subject: science

questions.question: Why do living things need food?
options: For energy and to grow, repair, and stay healthy
questions.explanation: Food provides energy for daily activities and contains nutrients needed for growth, repair, and staying healthy.

questions.question: Which nutrient gives us the MOST energy?
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates are the body's main energy source — found in rice, bread, pasta, potatoes.

questions.question: Which food group helps build and repair muscles?
questions.explanation: Proteins are building blocks for muscles, organs, and cells. Found in meat, fish, eggs, beans, nuts.

questions.question: Why do we need vitamins?
options: To keep the body working well and prevent disease
questions.explanation: Vitamins help the body function properly and protect against diseases. Different vitamins have different roles.

questions.question: Vitamin C is found mainly in:
questions.explanation: Vitamin C is in citrus fruits, strawberries, and vegetables. It helps the immune system and wound healing.

questions.question: What is a balanced diet?
options: Eating different types of food in the right amounts for good health
questions.explanation: A balanced diet includes the right amounts of all food groups — carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, and water.

questions.question: Calcium is important for:
questions.explanation: Calcium builds and maintains strong bones and teeth. Found in milk, cheese, yoghurt, and leafy greens.

questions.question: Why should we drink plenty of water every day?
options: Water keeps the body hydrated, helps digestion, and removes waste
Water is only needed in summer
questions.explanation: Water is essential for life — it keeps cells hydrated, aids digestion, regulates temperature, and removes waste.

questions.question: Which food is NOT a good source of protein?
questions.explanation: White rice is mainly a carbohydrate — not high in protein. Eggs, chicken, and lentils are good protein sources.

questions.question: Fibre in food helps:
questions.explanation: Fibre helps food move through the digestive system and prevents constipation. Found in fruits, vegetables, and wholegrain foods.

questions.question: Too much sugar in our diet can lead to:
options: Tooth decay and increased risk of obesity and diabetes
questions.explanation: Excessive sugar causes tooth decay (cavities) and can lead to obesity and type 2 diabetes.

questions.question: Iron is an important mineral that helps:
questions.explanation: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin in red blood cells, which carries oxygen around the body.

questions.question: Which of these is a healthy snack?
questions.explanation: An apple (vitamins, fibre) and nuts (protein, healthy fats) are nutritious snacks. Crisps, chocolate, and fizzy drinks are high in sugar, salt, or unhealthy fats.

questions.question: Digestion begins in the:
questions.explanation: Digestion begins in the mouth — teeth grind food and saliva starts breaking down carbohydrates.

questions.question: Which vitamin helps our eyes see well in low light?
questions.explanation: Vitamin A helps maintain good vision, especially in dim light. Found in carrots, sweet potato, and leafy greens.
